why: Teaching AI use in courses vs career-readiness rationale vs institutional AI literacy.

options.name: Teaching AI use in courses
options.covers: Learning to use AI effectively is a professional skill employers expect; courses teach or demonstrate AI use.

options.name: Career and workplace readiness as a reason to learn AI
options.covers: Preparing students for an AI-shaped workplace as the rationale for teaching or allowing AI (split from P44, which keeps teaching AI use in courses).

options.name: AI literacy training and resources
options.covers: The institution offers or mandates AI-literacy training, modules, guides or curricular AI-literacy for students, staff or the whole community. Faculty-only support is P63. Evidence: Georgia Southern, Kennesaw State, Clark, East Tennessee State, Florida International, Brown, Baylor, Cleveland State.

options.name: Prompting advice
options.covers: Practical advice on writing prompts or probing AI tools to get better results or learn their limits. Evidence: Pepperdine, Oakland, Sam Houston State, Santa Clara, San Diego State, NC State.

units.passage: Emphasize that critical thinking, evaluation of information, and digital literacy are essential skills that extend beyond the classroom and into the workforce.
units.why: Asks instructors to tell students critical thinking and digital literacy matter for work. The career argument is about skills: P44, with a fit note.

units.passage: Since students are likely to encounter AI tools in the workplace
units.why: Gives the workplace reason for including AI in assessment: P44, learning to use AI as a professional skill.

units.passage: Teaching students how to brainstorm with generative AI can help students how to effectively use it and where it can be most effective
units.why: 'Teaching students how to brainstorm with generative AI can help students how to effectively use it' supports AI for brainstorming: P15.

units.passage: 73% of employers use GenAI while more than half (55%) of graduates said their program did not prepare them to use GenAI tools during their studies
units.why: '73% of employers use GenAI while more than half (55%) of graduates said their program did not prepare them' is cited to argue that students need AI skills for work: P44.

units.passage: For faculty, this means moving beyond awareness to active engagement with AI tools in order to prepare students for a workforce that already demands AI literacy
units.why: 'moving beyond awareness to active engagement with AI tools in order to prepare students for a workforce that already demands AI literacy' tells faculty to engage with AI for career reasons: P44.

units.passage: Frame AI as a professional skill and ethical responsibility. Ask students: When is it helpful? When is it harmful?
units.why: 'Frame AI as a professional skill and ethical responsibility' asks instructors to present AI as a professional skill: P44.

units.passage: You can use class lecture time or prepare instructional videos demonstrating what effective and appropriate use of AI looks like for class activities. Allow students to reflect on what they observe and practice what you demonstrate, and provide guidance and feedback.
units.why: Instructors can use 'class lecture time or prepare instructional videos demonstrating what effective and appropriate use of AI looks like': teaching AI use, P44.

units.passage: However, you may also find it helpful to design opportunities for students to develop AI literacy by incorporating generative AI into your teaching.
units.why: "design opportunities for students to develop AI literacy by incorporating generative AI into your teaching" suggests teaching with AI to build literacy; P44 (teach effective AI use), as an option.

units.passage: As we prepare students for their future role in society, Villanova has an obligation to equip students and graduates, as well as employees and researchers, with the tools they need to navigate in a world with emerging and rapidly changing technologies.
units.why: The purpose section says Villanova "has an obligation to equip students and graduates" with tools for a world of emerging technologies; this is a career-readiness rationale, so P44, informs, general.

units.passage: SDS faculty are encouraged to teach students how to thoughtfully and ethically incorporate AI tools to maximize student learning while ensuring that faculty can assess competency against course learning outcomes.
units.policy: SDS faculty are encouraged to teach students how to thoughtfully and ethically incorporate AI tools to maximize learning while ensuring they can assess competency against course learning outcomes.
units.why: "SDS faculty are encouraged to teach students how to thoughtfully and ethically incorporate AI tools". Teaching AI use as a skill while keeping assessment of competency, P44.

units.passage: It is important that they learn how to use them appropriately and that they understand these tools’ limitations and the ethical issues connected with their use.
units.policy: It is important that students learn how to use Gen-AI tools appropriately and understand their limitations and the ethical issues connected with their use.
units.why: "It is important that they learn how to use them appropriately and that they understand these tools' limitations" gives learning to use AI well as a reason for teaching it. P44.

units.passage: AI is changing how legal research is conducted, and Daniel's course necessarily has to respond to those changes to be effective in preparing his students for their legal careers.
units.why: The course "necessarily has to respond to those changes to be effective in preparing his students for their legal careers"; teaching AI tools as a professional skill (P44).

units.passage: Students may be expected to possess the skills and competencies to effectively utilize Gen AI in their courses, as well as the various organizations they join upon graduating.
units.why: "Students may be expected to possess the skills and competencies to effectively utilize Gen AI in their courses" and in later employment frames AI use as a skill expected by employers, so P44.

units.passage: As such, it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy, as well as remain aware of its potential drawbacks and limitations.
units.why: "it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy, as well as remain aware of its potential drawbacks and limitations" recommends AI literacy for the community; closest is P44 (AI use as skill) though it also names limitations.

units.passage: Consequently, it is imperative to help our students develop AI literacy-- including its potential risks-- so that students are equipped with practical AI literacy skills required for future careers.
units.why: The sentence says 'it is imperative to help our students develop AI literacy ... required for future careers', a should-level direction to faculty to teach AI use as a career skill, so P44, instructor, before-course, should.

units.passage: For courses where Gen AI is included in course curriculum, it is expected that both instructors and students understand how to use these resources effectively, appropriately, and ethically, while also remaining mindful of both its usefulness and its limitations.
units.why: "it is expected that both instructors and students understand how to use these resources effectively, appropriately, and ethically" sets a general expectation for courses that include Gen AI; closest to P44 (effective use as a skill).

units.passage: Acknowledge the growing importance of AI in the world today, and in your field.
units.why: Developing-a-policy advice says to 'Acknowledge the growing importance of AI in the world today, and in your field': teaching AI as an expected skill (P44).

units.passage: If appropriate, explain how students will be encouraged to learn with AI to prepare them for careers.
units.why: Instructors should 'explain how students will be encouraged to learn with AI to prepare them for careers': career-skill rationale (P44).

units.passage: Generative AI tools are becoming increasingly influential across many industries, making it important for students to understand how to use these tools within their specific fields of study.
units.why: 'Making it important for students to understand how to use these tools within their specific fields' is a career/professional-skill reason (P44).

units.passage: Identify the skills and approaches necessary to use GAI successfully in relevant fields, disciplines, or professions.
units.policy: Programs identify the skills and approaches necessary to use GAI successfully in relevant fields, disciplines, or professions, and how fields and professions use GAI that students should learn about.
units.why: Asks what skills students need 'to use GAI successfully in relevant fields, disciplines, or professions', treating AI use as a professional skill (P44).

units.passage: AI use is allowed on some assignments to give you experience working with these tools to supplement and grow your own knowledge.
units.why: 'AI use is allowed on some assignments to give you experience working with these tools': experience with AI as a skill, P44.

units.passage: In this course, AI use is permitted in specific assignments and activities to help you learn how to leverage these tools professionally while building your own capabilities
units.why: Permitting AI 'to help you learn how to leverage these tools professionally' gives a career-skill reason, P44.

units.passage: There may be a need to integrate AI literacy into certain curricula given employer demands and/or industry trends.
units.why: The report says AI literacy may need to be integrated into curricula "given employer demands and/or industry trends", a career reason to teach AI (P44).

units.passage: the restrictions you impose may hinder the development of skills and behaviors needed to engage thoughtfully in an AI-integrated world.
units.why: The page warns that 'the restrictions you impose may hinder the development of skills and behaviors needed to engage thoughtfully in an AI-integrated world'. It is a reason, addressed to instructors who are deciding what to impose, so it is rationale (informs) under P44 (effective AI use as a skill).

units.passage: The approach to AI use in this course and the inclusion of this acknowledgement in our work will help us to develop our skills for using AI while maintaining our academic integrity.
units.why: The sample says the approach "will help us to develop our skills for using AI while maintaining our academic integrity"; a reason that learning to use AI is a skill alongside integrity, P44.

units.passage: William & Mary cannot ignore the influence of GenAI in the modern world as employers are increasingly looking for graduates skilled in AI to help improve the efficiency of the workplace
units.why: 'employers are increasingly looking for graduates skilled in AI' is the career argument for learning AI, so P44 (professional skill); informs.

units.passage: The alumni emphasized that understanding AI fundamentals should be a baseline skill for new graduates
units.why: 'understanding AI fundamentals should be a baseline skill for new graduates' is the alumni argument that AI skill is expected in work, P44.

units.passage: As William & Mary stands at this crossroads, the imperative is clear: developing comprehensive AI literacy across students, faculty, and staff is not just a competitive advantage, but a necessary foundation for academic excellence, workforce readiness, and informed citizenship in the age
units.why: 'developing comprehensive AI literacy across students, faculty, and staff is not just a competitive advantage, but a necessary foundation' calls AI literacy essential for careers and citizenship, P44.

units.passage: Capstone and career focus: Encourages departments to incorporate AI modules in senior projects, internships, and co-curricular career development programs
units.why: 'Encourages departments to incorporate AI modules in senior projects, internships' integrates AI into coursework as a professional skill (P44); admin, before-course, should; encourage.

units.passage: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee is committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary to sustain success in an AI-driven world
units.why: The intro says UWM "is committed to providing students with the knowledge, skills and experience necessary to sustain success in an AI-driven world", a career-readiness rationale for engaging with AI, so P44 (informs).

units.passage: But students should also learn how knowledge is made and shared in their disciplines and in settings beyond the university, and how these methods may change in light of AI.
units.why: "students should also learn how knowledge is made and shared in their disciplines ... and how these methods may change in light of AI" gives a rationale that students learn AI-shaped professional methods, P44.

units.passage: we understand that students must be prepared to lead in an AI-infused world.
units.why: "students must be prepared to lead in an AI-infused world" gives preparation for AI-rich work as a reason to engage with AI: P44.

units.passage: Yale has the opportunity to serve as a model by adapting its curricula to prepare students to lead in advancing and considering the implications of AI.
units.why: "Yale has the opportunity to serve as a model by adapting its curricula to prepare students to lead" is an aspiration to prepare students for AI-rich work: P44.

units.passage: Protect academic integrity while helping students build the AI skills their future careers will require.
units.why: The bullet says to help students "build the AI skills their future careers will require", a career-readiness reason (P44).

units.passage: Develop responsible AI fluency appropriate to each discipline: the ability to use AI productively, evaluate and verify its output, recognize its limits, protect sensitive information, and take responsibility for work produced with its assistance.
units.why: The bullet aims at "responsible AI fluency": using AI productively, verifying output, taking responsibility; teaching effective AI use as a skill (P44).

units.passage: At the same time, AI is an important technology, and learning to use it well is part of preparing for your career.
units.why: "learning to use it well is part of preparing for your career" is a professional-skill reason to teach AI use (P44).

units.passage: Where AI use is appropriate, instructors are encouraged to place it in authentic disciplinary and professional contexts, so that students learn to use and evaluate AI in settings resembling those they will encounter beyond the classroom.
units.why: "instructors are encouraged to place it in authentic disciplinary and professional contexts" encourages teaching AI in professional settings (P44).
